From the ReactiveMicro TWGS Wiki page:

The TransWarp GS (TWGS) from Applied Engineering (AE) is considered by most to be the best and most expandable of the accelerator cards produced for the Apple IIgs. With its 32k of cache and upgradable clock this card is definitely a must have for every Apple IIgs user. Originally released as a 7 MHz accelerator it is now possible to modify some boards up to 18+ MHz.

AE released the TransWarp GS in the winter of 1988. The board came stock at 7MHz and 8k cache. They also offered an upgraded board to 8MHz and 32k cache board. The limiting factor to speed at the time was the "buggy" 816 CPU die. Later Western Design Center (WDC) worked with Sanyo to redesign the die, and the CPU speeds easily reached 10MHz. By this time however AE was out of business. About mid 1996 Joachim Lange (SHH Systeme), a hobbyist, created a new version of the 32k Cache Card for the TransWarp GS. Together with the redesigned '816 CPU some TransWarp GS users were able to reach 12MHz or better. On January 27th, 2006 Henry from ReActiveMicro announced on CSA2 the successful cracking and copying of the TransWarp GS GALs, and their release for sale and download. Henry discovered that using the redesigned '816 CPU, SHH Systeme's 32k Cache Card, and the last known revision of the GALs that his TransWarp GS reached 18.75MHz and was stable running most software. Shortly after this announcement ReActiveMicro started to offer upgrade services for users to send in their boards. In March 2007 ReActiveMicro created a 32k Cache Card which used 12ns SRAMs and allowed for more stable operation above 16MHz. In September 2014 work began on the TWGS v1.0 clone project from Ultimate-Micro. On May 4th, 2018 Henry decided to revist the TWGS v1.0 project and ReActiveMicro offered a presale opportunity for the TWGS v1.0 project, later incrementing the project to v1.1.

I finally received my TWGS v1.1 card and have had a chance to 'take her around the block' so to speak.

For something as complicated as this, installation was incredibly simple. The card goes in your slot 3. My slot 3 was already populated with A2RetroSystem's Uthernet II, which I'll also do a few type-ups on. The Uthernet II has moved over to slot 2. Once installed into slot, the card's speed is activated through classic desk accessories (Apple key+Ctrl+Esc). That was it, I'm now IIGS'ing at 16 Mhz.

On the downside of installation, however, if your TWGS card has it's fan installed (the boys at ReActiveMicro were kind enough to install a fan on mine for me), you won't be able to install anything into slot 4 because the fan intrudes into this area. For TWGS speeds of 16 MHz or higher, they are recommending use of the fan.

I've tried a couple pieces of software so far:

GSOS: The GSOS software is not such a pain to use anymore. Boot up time with 10+ desk accessories went from minutes to seconds. Everything is responsive, even while running an application with multiple windows open. I get the feeling of "I can actually do work with this thing, if only my ImageWriter II would work properly!" Well.. that's another project for another day..

Silpheed (Game): On a stock IIGS, the intro scene to this game runs at what seems to be 0.5 frames per second. With TWGS, the animation seems to be a sort-of-smooth 10-15 frames per second. Animation not as fluid as my 80286 machines running this same game, but still a marked improvement. Gameplay doesn't seem to be affected.. the game plays well on a stock IIGS as well as with TWGS installed. No noticeable difference.

Wolfenstein 3D (game): Fuck my life. The whole reason I bought this card was to play this game. Sure, frame rate is great. The game SEEMS to suffer timing issues registering key presses on keyboard. Mouse works just fine. Keyboard does NOT.. you'll find you'll need to press a key 10 times before it does anything at all, IF it chooses to do anything. I'm not an Apple IIGS expert at all, so I have no clue what is really going on with this. All I know is without TWGS, at least the game registers keyboard key presses.

Crystal Quest (game): I'm including this game, because it works just fine on a stock IIGS. What about with a TWGS installed? No noticeable difference. It doesn't seem that the TWGS is speeding up games that are already fast enough on stock machines, or I haven't come across one that needs to be "slowed down" in order to play yet.

That is all I've had time to play with thus far. I'll write more shit when I do more shit.
